title: Save $25 on Burga Phone Accessories with $50+ Order Sale
content: Burga is currently offering a $25 discount on orders exceeding $50. This sale applies to a range of phone accessories, including phone cases, magnetic rings, Apple Watch bands, and power banks.
summary: Burga is offering a $25 discount on orders over $50 for phone accessories. Eligible items include phone cases, magnetic rings, Apple Watch bands, and power banks.
author: Wired

title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Now $699.99, $100 Off, Matching All-Time Low Price
content:
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is currently available for $699.99 at Amazon, representing a $100 discount from its standard price of $799. This sale brings the smartwatch to its all-time low price point across multiple color options. As the most capable smartwatch in Apple’s lineup, the Ultra 4 is designed for users seeking extensive tracking capabilities or the longest battery life among Apple Watch models.

Powered by Apple’s S11 chip, which is also featured in the Series 12, the Ultra 4 offers faster performance than the previous generation. The device includes new Apple Intelligence features such as Sound Recognition, which alerts users to noises like alarms and doorbells. It also supports the Live Rewind feature, allowing users to revisit the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation. Additionally, an upcoming Siri Recap feature will generate summaries of conversations for later reference.

Health and fitness capabilities have been expanded in this model compared to previous versions. The sensors provide more accurate EKG measurements, and the watch can track heart rate as frequently as every five seconds. A new Readiness feature, which is not available on the Ultra 3 or earlier models, analyzes recent activity, sleep quality, and other health metrics to generate a score from zero to 10. This score helps users determine whether to push their physical limits or take it easy.

Hardware improvements include a battery that Apple promises will last up to 50 hours on a single charge, which is twice the duration of the Series 12. The Ultra 4 features Apple’s brightest watch display and a rugged design that is water-resistant up to 100 meters and IP6X-rated for dust resistance. The device retains the second-generation Ultra Wideband chip for Precision Finding and includes gesture controls that allow users to perform actions with a double tap or a flick of the wrist.

Other deals mentioned in the report include Ugreen’s FineTrack2 Bluetooth tracker, which is on sale for $13.99 at Amazon. This soccer ball-shaped tracker features a non-rechargeable battery that lasts up to seven years and integrates with Apple’s Find My network. It includes a lanyard for attachment to keys or bags. Additionally, Apple’s official watch bands are available for up to 69 percent off at Woot, with the silicone Sport Band priced at $14.99, the Sport Loop at $19.99, and the Trail Loop at $34.99. Hoto’s Pulse 4-in-1 Cordless Staple Gun is also on sale for $69.99 at Amazon, featuring a built-in display for battery life and safe firing alerts, and it comes with 1,200 fasteners.
summary: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is on sale for $699.99 ($100 off) at Amazon, matching its all-time low price. The model includes the new S11 chip, Apple Intelligence features such as Sound Recognition and Live Rewind, and up to 50 hours of battery life.
author: The Verge

title: BMW to launch urban driver‑assist system in 2027
content:
BMW announced that it will expand its navigation‑guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments beginning in 2027. The first rollout will occur in Germany, with other markets to follow.  

The new Level 2 system will use the vehicle’s built‑in GPS navigation to steer, accelerate, and decelerate on both highways and city streets. In town, it can assist with lane changes, turns, yielding to other vehicles, and navigating roundabouts. Drivers must keep their eyes on the road and remain ready to take over at any moment.
summary: BMW to launch urban driver‑assist system in 2027.
author: The Verge

title: Google discovers 1.3 million Videostrong devices used as botnet
content:
Google announced that its Android manufacturing partner, Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology Co., secretly embedded a backdoor in 1.3 million Android TV devices to create a botnet. The company stated that these infected devices were used without owners’ knowledge for malicious activities, including ad fraud, data exfiltration, and routing unauthorized network traffic. Google characterized the backdoor and botnet as intentionally developed and operated for financial gain.

In response, Google dismantled the backdoor and cut ties with Videostrong. The manufacturer has been banned from building or selling certified Android devices or supplying software for them.
summary: A current Videostrong Android TV device. Google says one of its Android manufacturing partners secretly built a backdoor in 1.3 million devices and turned them into a botnet.
author: The Verge

title: Meta to End Quest 2 OS Updates in 2027
content:
Meta has announced that it will release the final operating system update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro virtual reality headsets by March 2027. This concluding update, designated as version 213, marks the end of major software support for these devices. Following this milestone, the company stated it will continue to provide security patches and critical bug fixes until the end of 2027. Additionally, developers will be able to submit applications compatible with the Quest 2 and Quest Pro through December 2027.

The announcement positions the Quest 3 and 3S as the new baseline for Meta’s VR gaming ecosystem. Meta is making this transition in anticipation of its upcoming VR Glasses, which are scheduled to launch in the spring of 2027. The company noted that the Quest 2 and Quest Pro have laid the foundation for its current hardware lineup.
summary: Meta will release the last OS update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro VR headsets by March 2027, with v213 as the final version. After that, Meta will ship security patches and critical bug fixes through the end of 2027, and apps can be submitted through December 2027.
author: The Verge

title: Apple posts record $57.58 billion iPhone revenue in Q4 despite no standard model
content:
Apple reported a record‑breaking fourth‑quarter iPhone revenue of $57.58 billion, a 17 percent increase over the same period last year, according to its earnings release posted on Monday. The company achieved the jump even though it did not introduce a new standard iPhone model during its latest refresh.

The growth followed the September launch of the iPhone 18 lineup, which featured the pricier iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models. Apple also raised prices on its older iPhone models at the same time. In addition, the company unveiled its first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, but preorder sales for that device were not included in the reported earnings.
summary: Apple reported $57.58 billion in iPhone revenue for the fourth quarter, a 17 percent increase from a year earlier. The rise followed the September launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, price hikes on older models, and the exclusion of iPhone Duo pre‑order sales from the report.
author: The Verge
